inputs.original_text: The “8 million” figure is the organizers’ claim, not an official count—and authorities haven’t provided one. Still, the headline is already doing its job: turning a sprawling set of events into a single show of supposedly overwhelming national opposition to Trump. The organizers say turnout beat October’s by about one million people and 600 events, but without an independent count, those numbers are also part of the messaging. This looks less like neutral reporting than a coordinated effort to manufacture political momentum and make dissent appear more unified and decisive than the evidence can establish.
inputs.modified_text: That “8 million” figure is just the organizers’ claim, and authorities still haven’t provided a count. That silence is convenient: it leaves the headline free to turn scattered events into a supposedly unified national wave against Trump. The organizers’ claims of about one million more people and 600 more events than in October are part of the same sales pitch, not independent verification. This looks like coordinated narrative-building—using scale and repetition to manufacture momentum and make opposition seem more decisive than the evidence shows.
